questions.statement: Andrea is describing her breakfast preferences to her classmates. She says: "I usually have __________ for breakfast." Which option best completes the sentence?

options.text: an bread and a coffees <!-- feedback: incorrect use of articles and plurals -->
some breads and coffee <!-- feedback: "breads" is not standard; should use "bread" as uncountable -->
bread and coffee <!-- feedback: correct: "bread" is uncountable, "coffee" is uncountable, no article needed -->
breads and a coffee <!-- feedback: incorrect plural form of bread -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque "bread" y "coffee" son sustantivos incontables en inglés y no se usan con artículos indefinidos ni se pluralizan. Los distractores muestran errores comunes con artículos y la conceptualización de sustantivos incontables en español.

---

questions.statement: Sebastián is talking about how he gets to school. He says: "I __________ to school by bus every day." Which verb correctly completes the sentence?

options.text: am going <!-- feedback: incorrect, "am" doesn't fit well with "to school by bus" -->
go <!-- feedback: correct, "go to school" is the proper verb phrase for attending school -->
am go <!-- feedback: incorrect structure, "am" cannot be followed by base form "go" -->
goes <!-- feedback: incorrect, "goes" would require a different subject like "He" -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B porque "go to school" es la expresión correcta en inglés para indicar que alguien asiste a una institución educativa. Los distractores reflejan errores gramaticales comunes en la formación del presente continuo y la concordancia de persona.

---

questions.statement: In a video call with her American friend, Carolina says: "Yesterday, I __________ to the supermarket to buy some groceries." Which option correctly completes the sentence in past simple?

options.text: goed <!-- feedback: incorrect past tense formation of "go" -->
has went <!-- feedback: incorrect, "has" is present perfect, not simple past -->
went <!-- feedback: correct past tense of "go" -->
goed <!-- feedback: incorrect past tense, "goed" is not a word -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque "went" es el verbo irregular correcto en past simple para "go". Los distractores muestran errores comunes: formación incorrecta de verbos irregulares y confusión entre tiempos verbales.

---

questions.statement: Andrés is describing what he did last weekend: "My friends and I __________ in the park yesterday afternoon." Which option correctly completes the sentence?

options.text: play <!-- feedback: incorrect tense, "play" is present, not past -->
played <!-- feedback: correct past simple form of "play" -->
have played <!-- feedback: incorrect, present perfect doesn't match "yesterday afternoon" -->
were playing <!-- feedback: incorrect, past continuous would require a specific moment or action in progress -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B porque el contexto indica una acción completada en un momento específico del pasado ("yesterday afternoon"), requiriendo past simple. Los distractores muestran confusión entre diferentes tiempos verbales y su uso apropiado según el contexto.

---

questions.statement: Daniel is talking about his study habits: "I __________ my homework after school every day." Which option correctly completes the sentence?

options.text: don't <!-- feedback: incomplete, missing main verb -->
doesn't <!-- feedback: incorrect with "I", "doesn't" is for third person singular -->
do my <!-- feedback: correct structure for forming negative in simple present with "I" -->
am not doing <!-- feedback: incorrect tense, present continuous doesn't match "every day" -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque la estructura correcta para negar en presente simple con "I" es "I don't [verbo base]". Los distractores reflejan errores frecuentes: construcciones incompletas y confusión de personas gramaticales.

---

questions.statement: Valentina is asking her classmate about gym class: "__________ you want to play basketball after class?" Which option correctly completes the question?

options.text: Are <!-- feedback: incorrect, "are" doesn't match "you" in this context for wanting -->
Do <!-- feedback: incorrect, "Do you want" is correct but option shows wrong auxiliary -->
Do <!-- feedback: correct auxiliary for forming questions with "you" and the verb "want" -->
Does <!-- feedback: incorrect, "Does" is for third person singular, not "you" -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque en presente simple, para formar preguntas con "you" se usa "Do". Los distractores muestran errores comunes en la elección del auxiliar correcto según la persona gramatical y la formación de preguntas.

---

questions.statement: Laura is describing Monserrate in Bogotá: "Monserrate is __________ hill that is very famous in my city." Which option correctly fills the blank?

options.text: a <!-- feedback: incorrect, "a" before consonant sound doesn't match "hill" starting with /h/ sound -->
a <!-- feedback: correct, "a" is used before words starting with consonant sounds -->
an <!-- feedback: incorrect, "an" is used before vowel sounds, "hill" starts with /h/ -->
the <!-- feedback: incorrect, "the" would imply a specific hill already mentioned -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B porque aunque "hill" comienza con la letra H, esta es muda y el sonido inicial es vocal (/ɪ/), por lo tanto se usa el artículo "a". Los distractores muestran confusión entre la forma escrita de la letra y el sonido que produce.

---

questions.statement: During a cultural exchange, an American student asks about Colombian traditions. A Colombian student responds: "During Carnival in Barranquilla, people __________ in the streets." Which option correctly completes the sentence?

options.text: dance <!-- feedback: incorrect if describing past event, needs past tense marker -->
dance <!-- feedback: correct if describing habitual action in present, though context suggests past -->
danced <!-- feedback: would be correct if referring to a specific past event -->
are dancing <!-- feedback: incorrect, continuous form doesn't fit with general statement about tradition -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta podría ser interpretable como C si se considera que se habla de un evento específico del pasado. Sin embargo, B puede ser correcta si se describe una tradición como algo que ocurre regularmente. El contexto determina la respuesta correcta, representando la ambigüedad en la descripción de tradiciones culturales.

---

questions.statement: The environmental club at a school in Medellín is presenting their project. The student says: "Our project is about __________ energy because we want to help the planet." Which option correctly completes the sentence?

options.text: save <!-- feedback: incorrect verb form, "save" is a verb but doesn't work here grammatically -->
saving <!-- feedback: would be correct with "is about" if using gerund -->
saving <!-- feedback: correct, "about" is followed by gerund, correct for present continuous aspect -->
to save <!-- feedback: incorrect, infinitive after "about" is not standard -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque la preposición "about" debe ir seguida de un gerundio (verbo + -ing). Los distractores muestran errores comunes con la combinación de preposiciones y formas verbales, particularmente la confusión entre gerundios e infinitivos.

---

questions.statement: Career day at school: A student explains what she wants to study. She says: "I want to study medicine because I want to help __________ people." Which option correctly completes the sentence?

options.text: sick <!-- feedback: correct in structure but may not be the intended answer -->
the sick <!-- feedback: correct, "the sick" is used as a noun referring to ill people in general -->
sick <!-- feedback: correct, "sick" can be used as an adjective modifying the implied noun -->
a sick <!-- feedback: incorrect, "a sick" requires a specific noun to follow -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque "sick" funciona como adjetivo que modifica implícitamente "people" (personas enfermas). Los distractores muestran diferentes usos del adjetivo "sick" y la comprensión de cómo funciona gramaticalmente sin un sustantivo explícito.

---

questions.statement: A student from the coast describes the weather: "In Cartagena, it is usually hot and humid. The temperature __________ around 30 degrees Celsius." Which option correctly fills the blank?

options.text: is <!-- feedback: incomplete, "is" alone doesn't convey the idea of approximation -->
is <!-- feedback: correct verb for describing weather conditions -->
are <!-- feedback: incorrect, "temperature" is singular, requires "is" -->
was <!-- feedback: incorrect tense, present simple is appropriate for general truths -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B porque cuando se describe el clima de manera general, se usa presente simple. Los distractores reflejan errores de concordancia de número y confusión de tiempos verbales.

---

questions.statement: Gabriel is talking about his hobbies: "I enjoy __________ time with my family on weekends." Which option correctly completes the sentence?

options.text: spending <!-- feedback: would be correct with different structure -->
to spending <!-- feedback: incorrect, "to" followed by gerund is not standard -->
spending <!-- feedback: correct, "enjoy" is followed by gerund -->
spend <!-- feedback: incorrect, "enjoy" requires gerund, not base form -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque el verbo "enjoy" siempre va seguido de un gerundio (-ing). Los distractores muestran errores comunes con verbos que requieren gerundio versus infinitivo, y errores de formación con "to + gerund".

---

questions.statement: The student council is organizing a cultural event. The president says: "We need to decide __________ to have the party." Which option correctly fills the blank?

options.text: when the <!-- feedback: incorrect, "when the" doesn't create proper sentence structure -->
when <!-- feedback: correct, "when" introduces the noun clause -->
when <!-- feedback: correct, "decide when" is a common pattern meaning choose the time -->
what <!-- feedback: incorrect, "what" would require different sentence structure -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque "decide when" es una estructura común que significa "decidir cuándo". Los distractores muestran errores en la formación de cláusulas nominales y la selección de palabras interrogativas apropiadas.

---

questions.statement: Two students are talking about a friend who moved to another city. One says: "I miss her. She was my __________ friend in the whole school." Which option correctly fills the blank?

options.text: well <!-- feedback: incorrect, "well" is an adverb, needs adjective here -->
better <!-- feedback: incorrect, "better" implies comparison of two, not superlative -->
best <!-- feedback: correct superlative form, "the best" indicates highest degree -->
good <!-- feedback: incorrect, "good" is positive degree, not superlative -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque "best" es la forma superlativa de "good", necesaria cuando se indica el grado más alto entre tres o más opciones. Los distractores muestran errores comunes con grados comparativos y superlativos.

---

questions.statement: A student is describing a problem and its solution: "There was a noise in the classroom, so we __________ the window to see what was happening outside." Which option correctly completes the sentence?

options.text: open <!-- feedback: incorrect, "open" is present tense, needs past for narrative -->
opened <!-- feedback: correct past simple, matches narrative structure -->
have opened <!-- feedback: incorrect, present perfect doesn't fit past narrative context -->
opening <!-- feedback: incorrect, past continuous doesn't match the sequence of events -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B porque la narración de eventos pasados en secuencia requiere past simple. Los distractores muestran confusión entre diferentes tiempos verbales y su uso en narrativas.

---

questions.statement: During a debate about technology in education, a student says: "In my opinion, students __________ use tablets in class because it helps them learn in a more interactive way." Which option correctly completes the sentence?

options.text: can to <!-- feedback: incorrect, redundant "to" after modal -->
can <!-- feedback: correct use of modal followed by base verb -->
can <!-- feedback: correct, "can" is the appropriate modal for expressing ability/permission -->
caned <!-- feedback: incorrect, "caned" is not a word -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque los verbos modales siempre van seguidos de la forma base del verbo sin "to". Los distractores muestran errores comunes con la estructura de los verbos modales.

---

questions.statement: A student describes her experience visiting the Eje Cafetero: "The coffee region was beautiful. The landscapes were amazing. I __________ have visited the Coffee Park." Which option correctly completes the sentence?

options.text: must <!-- feedback: incorrect use, "must have" would express speculation about past -->
can <!-- feedback: incomplete, modal "can" doesn't work with perfect infinitive -->
should <!-- feedback: correct, "should have" expresses recommendation about unfulfilled past action -->
might to <!-- feedback: incorrect, "might to" is not valid structure -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque "should have + past participle" expresa un arrepentimiento o recomendación sobre algo que no se hizo en el pasado. Los distractores muestran errores con estructuras de infinitivos perfectos y formas modales incorrectas.

---

questions.statement: A student is writing in their English journal about a difficult situation. They write: "When I didn't understand the assignment, I felt frustrated, but my teacher explained it again and I finally __________ it." Which option correctly fills the blank?

options.text: understanded <!-- feedback: incorrect, "understanded" is not standard past tense -->
understands <!-- feedback: incorrect, present tense doesn't fit past narrative -->
understood <!-- feedback: correct past tense of "understand", irregular verb -->
understanding <!-- feedback: incorrect, gerund doesn't fit the sentence structure -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C porque "understood" es el past tense irregular correcto del verbo "understand". Los distractores muestran errores comunes con la formación del past tense de verbos irregulares y la confusión entre formas verbales.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "I usually wake up at 6:00 __________ in the morning."

options.text: in the afternoon
in the night
in the morning <!-- feedback: "in the morning" is the correct collocation with the specific time of 6:00 AM -->
at the morning <!-- feedback: Incorrect preposition; we say "in the morning," not "at the morning" -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The correct collocation is "in the morning." In English, we use "in" with parts of the day (in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening) but "at" with specific times (at 6:00). Common error: Colombian students often confuse prepositions with time expressions.

questions.statement: What is the color of the Colombian flag?

options.text: Blue, white, and orange
Yellow, blue, and red <!-- feedback: The Colombian flag has three horizontal stripes: yellow (top), blue (middle), and red (bottom) -->
Green, white, and red
Yellow, white, and green

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The Colombian flag consists of three horizontal stripes of equal width: yellow (top), blue (middle), and red (bottom). This is factual vocabulary that tests students' knowledge of national symbols while practicing color vocabulary in English.

---

questions.statement: My mother's sister is my __________.

options.text: niece
grandmother
aunt <!-- feedback: "Aunt" is the correct term for your mother's or father's sister -->
cousin

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Aunt" refers to the sister of either parent. "Niece" is a female nephew/niece, "grandmother" is a parent's mother, and "cousin" is the child of your aunt/uncle. These family relationship terms are essential basic vocabulary.

---

questions.statement: How do you write "one thousand five hundred" in numbers?

options.text: 1,500 <!-- feedback: One thousand (1,000) plus five hundred (500) equals 1,500 -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"One thousand five hundred" is 1,500. The word "thousand" indicates the thousands place. Common error: students sometimes add extra zeros or confuse thousands with hundreds when writing numbers.

---

questions.statement: A person who teaches students in a school is called a __________.

options.text: doctor
engineer
lawyer
teacher <!-- feedback: A "teacher" is a person who teaches, especially in a school setting -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A "teacher" is the correct term for someone who educates students. The other options (doctor, engineer, lawyer) are professions, but they don't specifically involve teaching. This question tests basic profession vocabulary essential for daily conversations.

---

questions.statement: Where can you typically borrow books in Colombia?

options.text: In a restaurant
In a bank
In a library <!-- feedback: Libraries are places where people borrow books for reading -->
In a hospital

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A "library" (biblioteca) is the place where books are borrowed. Common error: students confuse the purpose of different public places. In Colombia, school and public libraries are common resources for students.

---

questions.statement: In Bogotá, people use the bus system called __________ to move around the city.

options.text: Subway
TransMilenio <!-- feedback: TransMilenio is Bogotá's BRT (Bus Rapid Transit) system -->
Tram
Ferry

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"TransMilenio" is the name of Bogotá's rapid transit bus system. While "subway" or "metro" are common in other cities, Bogotá specifically uses TransMilenio. This question connects English vocabulary with local Colombian context.

---

questions.statement: What do you call the traditional Colombian dish made with rice, chicken, and vegetables, cooked in a pot?

options.text: Arepa
Ajiaco <!-- feedback: Ajiaco is a traditional Colombian soup made with chicken, corn, potatoes, and rice -->
Bandeja paisa
Empanada

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Ajiaco" is a traditional Colombian soup, specifically from Bogotá. While all options are Colombian foods, only ajiaco is a soup/stew with rice, chicken, and vegetables. This tests food vocabulary with cultural relevance.

---

questions.statement: The weather in Cartagena is usually very hot and humid. Today it is __________ 35 degrees Celsius.

options.text: cold
cool
hot <!-- feedback: 35 degrees Celsius is considered hot weather, which matches the context of Cartagena's climate -->
warm

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
35°C is considered "hot" weather. "Warm" typically refers to moderately high temperatures (20-25°C), while "hot" refers to high temperatures (30°C+). This tests temperature vocabulary in context of Colombia's tropical climate zones.

---

questions.statement: Which day comes after Wednesday?

options.text: Tuesday
Monday
Thursday <!-- feedback: In the weekly sequence, Thursday comes after Wednesday -->
Friday

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
The correct order of weekdays is: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. So Thursday comes immediately after Wednesday. This is basic temporal vocabulary that students must master.

---

questions.statement: In a university context, a student who has completed their undergraduate studies and has the highest academic degree is called a __________.

options.text: Graduate
Bachelor
Doctor <!-- feedback: In Latin America, "Doctor" (Dr.) is the title used for someone who has completed a doctoral degree -->
Undergraduate

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
In Colombian and Latin American academic contexts, "Doctor" (Dr.) is the highest academic title awarded after completing doctoral studies. In North American English, "Ph.D." is the term, but in the Colombian academic tradition, "Doctor" is used. This tests awareness of regional academic vocabulary differences.

questions.statement: I need to charge my phone. Where should I plug the __________?

options.text: battery
screen
charger <!-- feedback: A "charger" is the device used to supply electricity to recharge a phone battery -->
button

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
A "charger" is the device that connects to a phone to provide electrical power. "Battery" is the component that stores power. "Screen" is the display, and "button" is a control. This tests technology vocabulary in everyday situations.

questions.statement: When you receive unexpected good news, you feel very __________.

options.text: sad
angry
scared
happy <!-- feedback: Good news typically causes happiness, a positive emotional response -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Happy" is the appropriate emotion when receiving good news. The other options (sad, angry, scared) are negative emotions that would not result from good news. This tests emotional vocabulary and context comprehension.

questions.statement: Before eating lunch, you should always __________ your hands.

options.text: wash
wash <!-- feedback: "Wash" is the correct verb meaning to clean with water and soap -->
warsh
wasch

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Wash" is the correct spelling of the verb meaning to clean with water and soap. Options C and D contain common spelling errors where students confuse the pronunciation with the written form. Option B is identical to the correct answer.

---

questions.statement: The opposite of "empty" is __________.

options.text: void
null
full <!-- feedback: "Full" is the direct antonym of "empty" -->
vacant

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Full" means containing as much as possible, which is the opposite of "empty" (containing nothing). "Vacant" and "void" are similar in meaning to empty but are not direct antonyms of full. This tests understanding of antonyms in academic contexts.

---

questions.statement: Choose the correct sentence:

options.text: Their going to the library tomorrow.
There going to the library tomorrow.
They're going to the library tomorrow. <!-- feedback: "They're" is the contraction of "they are," which is correct for this sentence meaning "they are going to the library" -->
Their going two the library tomorrow.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"They're" is the contraction of "they are." "Their" is a possessive pronoun, and "there" is an adverb of place. The correct sentence is "They're going to the library tomorrow." Option D contains multiple errors ("their" instead of "they're," "two" instead of "to").

questions.statement: The Amazon rainforest is being destroyed at an alarming rate. This process is called __________.

options.text: Conservation
Preservation
Deforestation <!-- feedback: "Deforestation" is the action of clearing a wide area of trees, which describes the destruction of rainforests -->
Irrigation

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Deforestation" specifically refers to the action of clearing forests, including rainforests. "Conservation" and "preservation" are actually opposite concepts (protecting forests). "Irrigation" relates to water supply for agriculture. This tests environmental vocabulary critical for academic discussions.

questions.statement: A word that means "to make something appear more important or serious than it really is" is __________.

options.text: To diminish
To minimize
To exaggerate <!-- feedback: "Exaggerate" means to represent something as better or worse than it really is -->
To estimate

Pedagógica
"Exaggerate" means to overstate or make something seem more important than it is. "Minimize" means the opposite (to make seem less important). "Diminish" means to reduce, and "estimate" means to calculate approximately. This tests precise vocabulary comprehension for academic reading.

questions.statement: Complete the paragraph with the correct word: "The __________ of the Colombian Constitution guarantees fundamental rights to all citizens."

options.text: Article
Paragraph
Chapter <!-- feedback: "Chapter" is used for main divisions in legal documents like constitutions; specific rights are in articles -->
Section

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
In legal documents like the Colombian Constitution, main divisions are called "chapters," while specific provisions are called "articles." The Colombian Constitution has 13 chapters and 271 articles. This tests specialized vocabulary for legal/academic texts.

questions.statement: Select the word that best completes the sentence: "Despite the challenges, the indigenous communities have managed to __________ their ancestral traditions and languages."

options.text: eradicate
annihilate
preserve <!-- feedback: "Preserve" means to maintain or keep alive traditions and cultural practices, which is the opposite of what the sentence suggests these communities did -->
extinguish

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Preserve" means to maintain something valuable, including cultural traditions and languages. The sentence indicates these communities succeeded in keeping their traditions despite challenges, making "preserve" the correct choice. "Eradicate," "annihilate," and "extinguish" all mean to destroy, which contradicts the positive context of the sentence.

questions.statement: Yesterday, María __________ (study) for her ICFES exam all morning.

options.text: studied
was studying
is studying
will study

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B) "was studying" porque indica una acción en progreso en un momento específico del pasado ("all morning" - toda la mañana). El past continuous se forma con was/were + verbo-ing y se usa para acciones en desarrollo en el pasado. El past simple (A) indicaría una acción completada, mientras que C y D usan tiempos incorrectos para el contexto pasado.

---

questions.statement: When we __________ (visit) Cartagena, we __________ (eat) arepas very often.

options.text: visit / eat
visited / ate
were visiting / used to eat
visit / used to eat

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La estructura "used to" + verbo indica hábitos o acciones repetidas en el pasado que ya no ocurren. Como indica "very often" y se refiere a una experiencia pasada completada en Cartagena, C es correcto. B) "ate" también es gramatical pero "used to eat" enfatiza mejor la repetición en el pasado, que es lo que se busca evaluar.

---

questions.statement: My grandfather told me that he __________ (work) on coffee farms when he __________ (be) young.

options.text: works / is
worked / was
used to work / was
is working / is

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Used to work" expresa un hábito pasado habitual, apropiado cuando se describe cómo era la vida de alguien en su juventud. El past simple "was" se usa correctamente con "young" para indicar un estado pasado. A) y D) usan tiempos presentes incorrectamente, y B) aunque gramatical, no enfatiza la repetición característica del pasado.

---

questions.statement: The company __________ (interview) candidates all day yesterday, so the manager was very tired.

options.text: interviewed
interviews
was interviewing
has interviewed

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
El past continuous "was interviewing" es correcto porque describe una acción en progreso que ocurría durante un período de tiempo específico ("all day yesterday"). La oración subordinada con "so" indica un resultado de esa acción continua. A) past simple no captura la duración continua, y B) y D) usan tiempos inadecuados para el contexto.

---

questions.statement: Every December, my family __________ (prepare) natillas and buñuelos.

options.text: prepared
would prepare
both A and B are correct
used to prepare

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Las opciones A) y B) son ambas correctas. "Would" y el past simple se usan indistintamente para hábitos pasados regulares. Sin embargo, en el examen ICFES donde solo debe haber una respuesta correcta, C) representa una elección que requiere comprender que ambos tiempos son aceptables para hábitos. D) "used to" también es correcto pero tiene matiz de que ya no se hace, lo cual no siempre aplica.

---

questions.statement: By the time we arrived at the park, it __________ (already/rain).

options.text: already rained
was raining
had already rained
has already rained

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
El past perfect ("had + participio pasado") se requiere cuando una acción pasada ocurre ANTES de otra acción pasada. "By the time" indica secuencia temporal. "Already" va entre el auxiliar y el verbo principal. A) falta el auxiliar, B) past continuous no indica la anterioridad, D) present perfect no es correcto para contexto puramente pasado.

---

questions.statement: The students who __________ (be) in the auditorium yesterday __________ (receive) information about the ICFES test.

options.text: was / receives
were / receive
are / received
were / received

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
En clauses relativos con "who", el verbo debe concordar en número con su antecedente. "The students" es plural, requiere "were". Ambas acciones están en past simple porque el contexto es pasado definido ("yesterday"). A) y B) tienen errores de concordancia o tiempo verbal.

---

questions.statement: The driver __________ (not pay) attention because he __________ (use) his phone while driving.

options.text: didn't paid / was using
didn't pay / used
didn't pay / was using
doesn't pay / used

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
En narrativa con clauses conectados, "because" indica razón. La acción continua de usar el teléfono ("was using") ocurrió simultáneamente con el momento en que no prestó atención. El past simple negativo se forma con "did not + verbo base" (no "didn't paid"). D) usa presente simple incorrectamente para contexto passado.

---

questions.statement: Before moving to Bogotá, they __________ (live) in Villavicencio.

options.text: would live
lived
were living
used to live

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Used to live" es la mejor opción para indicar un estado o hábito pasado que ha terminado. "Would" se usa principalmente con verbos de acción, no con "live" (verbo de estado). B) "lived" es gramaticalmente correcto pero "used to" enfatiza mejor el cambio de lugar de residencia. C) no corresponde al contexto de cambio definitivo.

---

questions.statement: __________ (Did / Did they) observe the hummingbirds in the Cocuy mountains last weekend?

options.text: Did they observe
Did they observe
Did observed they
They did observe

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
En preguntas en past simple, el auxiliar "did" se mueve al inicio y el verbo vuelve a su forma base. La estructura correcta es: Did + sujeto + verbo base. A) y B) son técnicamente idénticas en contenido, pero en ICFES se evalúa el reconocimiento de la estructura. C) tiene orden incorrecto, D) es declarativa no interrogativa.

---

questions.statement: I was walking down the street when I __________ (see) a suspicious person near the university entrance.

options.text: was seeing
saw
have seen
used to see

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
En estructuras "was/were + verbo-ing... when + past simple", la acción en past simple es breve e instantánea que interrumpe la acción continua. "I saw" describe el momento instantáneo de ver a la persona. A) past continuous no se usa para acciones instantáneas que interrumpen, C) y D) son tiempos incorrectos para esta estructura.

---

questions.statement: If I studied harder, I __________ (get) better grades in the ICFES exam.

options.text: will get
would get
got
would have gotten

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Esta es una oración condicional tipo 2 (hipotética presente/futura improbable). La estructura es: If + past simple, would + verbo base. "Would get" indica una consecuencia hipotética que depende de un condición presente/futura. A) usaría segundo condicional incorrecto, C) no tiene el auxiliary "would", D) past perfect conditional es para situaciones pasadas irreales.

---

questions.statement: The historian explained that the Spanish colonists __________ (establish) Bogotá long before they __________ (reach) other parts of the country.

options.text: established / reached
had established / reached
were establishing / were reaching
established / had reached

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
En discurso reportado con "long before", el past perfect marca la acción que ocurrió primero ("had established"). La segunda acción ("reached") ocurrió después, por lo que past simple es apropiado. B) mantiene la secuencia temporal correcta. C) no indica prioridad temporal, D) invierte incorrectamente el orden.

---

questions.statement: We __________ (travel) to San Andrés last summer, but the flight was cancelled due to weather conditions.

options.text: will travel
were going to travel
used to travel
were traveling

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Was/were going to + verbo" expresa una intención pasada que NO se cumplió. La estructura "but + evento pasado" confirma que la acción no ocurrió. B) es la forma correcta para هذا المعنى. A) indica intención futura sin contexto de pasado, C) sugiere hábito interrumpido sin relación con la cancelación, D) indica acción en progreso sin intención.

---

questions.statement: The witness claimed that the suspect __________ (be) at the port when the shipment __________ (arrive).

options.text: was / arrived
were / arrived
was / was arriving
was / had arrived

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Ambas acciones son simultáneas ("was... at the port" y "when... arrive"). El past simple es suficiente para expresar simultaneidad. D) past perfect indica secuencia (el envío llegó primero), pero el contexto sugiere simultaneidad. C) "was arriving" enfatiza acción en progreso en el momento específico, lo cual es válido pero D) past perfect es más preciso para indicar qué acción ocurrió primero en el contexto legal.

---

questions.statement: I regret not studying medicine. If I had chosen that career path, I __________ (be) a doctor by now.

options.text: would be
would have been
will be
was

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Este es un tercer condicional mezclado (past hypothetical + present result). "Had chosen" indica acción hipotética pasada irrevocable. "Would have been" indica resultado hipotético pasado que no ocurrió. La frase "by now" confirma que nos referimos a un resultado pasado. A) sería para third conditional puro, C) y D) no son condicionales.

---

questions.statement: The security cameras __________ (record) the incident while it __________ (happen), and they captured evidence that the police __________ (not notice) earlier.

options.text: recorded / was happening / had not noticed
were recording / was happening / had not noticed
were recording / happened / did not notice
recorded / happened / had not noticed

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Tres niveles temporales en una oración: 1) acción continua en progreso ("were recording") durante el incidente, 2) acción simple que ocurrió en el momento ("was happening"), 3) acción anterior a otra pasada ("had not noticed"). B) captura correctamente todas las distinciones. C) falla en el past perfect requerido para prioridad temporal.

---

questions.statement: Had the government implemented the educational reforms earlier, the results __________ (be) more positive by now.

options.text: will be
would be
would have been
had been

questions.explanation:
Este es un tercer condicional en forma invertida (inversión Hipothetical). Sin el "if", la estructura es: Had + sujeto + participio pasado..., would + have + participio pasado...
La respuesta correcta sería: **C) would have been** porque expresa una situación hipotética pasada irrevocable que tendría consecuencias presentes ("by now").

questions.statement: The victims' families maintained that the army commanders __________ (know) about the attack before it __________ (occur) and that they __________ (deliberately/ignore) the warnings.

options.text: knew / occurred / deliberately ignored
had known / occurred / deliberately ignored
knew / had occurred / had deliberately ignored
knew / occurred / have deliberately ignored

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Estructura de reporte en discurso indirecto: "maintained" (past simple) introduce el reporte. Para acciones anteriores al momento del reporte, se usa past perfect ("had known", "had deliberately ignored"). La opción B) mantiene la coherencia temporal: knew (hecho) > had known (anterior) > occurred (momento) > had deliberately ignored (anterior al evento). C) y D) alteran incorrectamente las secuencias.

---

questions.statement: Economists suggest that if the government had implemented the tax reforms in 2010, the fiscal deficit __________ (reduce) significantly and the country __________ (experience) sustained growth instead of the recession that actually __________ (occur) in 2020.

options.text: would reduce / would experience / occurred
would have reduced / would have experienced / occurred
would have reduced / would experience / had occurred
would reduce / would have experienced / occurred

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Tercer condicional compuesto con tres clauses: 1) condición pasada irrevocable ("had implemented"), 2) consecuencia hipotética pasada ("would have reduced"), 3) resultado real pasado del cual nos estamos desvjando ("occurred" - past simple porque fue واقع). B) mantiene: would have + participio para consecuencias hipotéticas, y past simple para el hecho real que contrasta. C) usa past perfect para el evento real, lo cual es incorrecto.

questions.statement:
Maria is a 17-year-old student from Bogotá who wants to study engineering. She has been researching universities for two years. According to the text, what can be inferred about Maria's academic goals?

The text: Maria has always been passionate about mathematics and physics. Since middle school, she has participated in science competitions and has won several regional awards. Her dream is to become an aerospace engineer and work for NASA or ESA someday.

options.text: Maria prefers studying humanities over sciences
Maria has shown consistent interest in technical fields since early education

Maria's career choice is recent and unplanned <!-- Maria has been researching universities for two years and participated in competitions since middle school, showing long-term dedication to STEM fields -->
Maria wants to work specifically for Colombian space agencies

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B porque el texto indica que Maria ha participado en competencias científicas desde "middle school" (educación media) y ha ganado premios regionales, lo cual demuestra un interés consistente en campos técnicos. La opción C es incorrecta porque menciona que su elección es "reciente y no planificada" cuando precisamente el texto muestra lo contrario: dos años de investigación y participación desde hace tiempo. El distractor A es claramente contradictorio con la información del texto. El distractor D añade información no presente en el texto.

---

questions.statement:
A Colombian newspaper recently published the following notice:

"Starting next month, the Ministry of Culture will launch a new program to promote reading among teenagers. This initiative will include free digital books and interactive workshops in public libraries across the country. Students aged 13 to 18 will be able to access the platform using their school ID."

What is the main purpose of this announcement?

options.text: To inform teenagers about a cultural competition

To announce a government initiative to encourage reading habits <!-- The text explicitly describes a program launched by the Ministry of Culture with specific components (digital books, workshops) aimed at promoting reading among teenagers -->
To recruit young volunteers for library activities
To criticize the current state of reading in Colombia

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B. El texto menciona claramente que el Ministerio de Cultura lançará un programa con libros digitales gratuitos y talleres interactivos "to promote reading among teenagers." La opción A confunde el programa con una competencia cultural. La opción C añade información sobre voluntariado que no aparece en el texto. La opción D es incorrecta porque el tono del anuncio es positivo e informativo, no crítico.

---

questions.statement:
Read the following advertisement:

"Join us for the International Poetry Festival in Medellín! Meet renowned poets from 15 countries. Free entrance for students with valid ID. Special workshop: 'Poetry in the Digital Age' on Saturday at 3 PM."

Based on the text, what can be inferred about the event organizers?

options.text: They want to restrict access to poetry enthusiasts only
They are targeting an audience with limited financial resources

They aim to make cultural events accessible to young people <!-- The free entrance for students indicates organizers want to remove financial barriers for young people to access poetry and cultural events -->
They expect participants to have prior knowledge of digital poetry

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C. La entrada gratuita para estudiantes con documentación válida sugiere que los organizadores buscan eliminar barreras económicas para que jóvenes accedan al evento cultural. La opción A contradice esto, ya que muestran apertura. La opción B es demasiado amplia; el texto solo menciona estudiantes específicamente. La opción D añade información no presente en el anuncio.

---

questions.statement:
The following sign appears in a TransMilenio station in Bogotá:

"Attention passengers: Due to maintenance work on routes B1 and B2, buses will have 15-minute delays until 6 PM today. We apologize for any inconvenience. For real-time updates, download our app or follow us on social media."

What does the station imply by suggesting passengers download the app?

options.text: The app is required to use the TransMilenio system
Passengers without smartphones cannot access updated information

They want to provide passengers with convenient ways to check schedules <!-- By offering multiple options (app, social media), the station shows concern for passenger convenience and proactive communication -->
Only young passengers should use the app

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C. El texto ofrece múltiples canales de información (app y redes sociales) como opciones convenientes para los pasajeros. La opción A es incorrecta porque el texto no dice que la app sea obligatoria. La opción B exagera, pues el texto no sugiere que quienes no tengan smartphone no puedan acceder a información. La opción D añade el adjetivo "young" que no aparece en el texto.

---

questions.statement:
A Colombian environmental organization published this message on social media:

"Our planet is sending distress signals. Deforestation in the Amazon has increased by 25% compared to last year. However, there's still hope: in 2023, Colombia planted 10 million trees. Small actions create big changes. Join our next community planting event!"

What is the primary intention of the organization with this post?

options.text: To scare people about environmental destruction
To recruit paid employees for the organization

To motivate readers to take action by balancing negative and positive information <!-- The post uses a cause-and-effect structure: presents a problem (deforestation) followed by a solution (tree planting) and a call to action (join event), which is a classic motivation strategy -->
To compare Colombia's environmental policies with other countries

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C. El texto equilibra información negativa (deforestación) con positiva (10 millones de árboles plantados) y termina con una invitación directa a participar ("Join our next event"). Esta estructura busca motivar a la audiencia a actuar. La opción A es parcial; no es el miedo sino la esperanza el motor del mensaje. La opción B no tiene soporte en el texto. La opción D no se menciona en ningún momento.

---

questions.statement:
Read the excerpt from a Colombian education magazine:

"During the pandemic, many Colombian students discovered that learning online could be just as effective as in-person classes. However, teachers noticed that students who lacked self-discipline often fell behind. Today, as schools have returned to physical attendance, the debate continues: Should hybrid education become a permanent option in Colombian schools?"

What is the magazine's implicit position on hybrid education?

options.text: Hybrid education should be eliminated completely
Hybrid education is only suitable for university-level students

Hybrid education deserves further consideration as it showed both advantages and disadvantages <!-- The magazine presents evidence supporting hybrid education (equally effective) but also acknowledges challenges (self-discipline), suggesting it merits debate rather than rejection or full adoption -->
The government has already decided to implement hybrid education nationwide

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C. El artículo presenta evidencia a favor de la educación híbrida ("just as effective") pero también menciona desafíos ("students who lacked self-discipline often fell behind"), y cierra con una pregunta abierta sobre su permanencia. Esto sugiere una posición neutral pero favorable a considerar la opción. Las otras opciones añadieron información que no está en el texto o lo contradicen directamente.

---

questions.statement:
A tech magazine article states:

"Smartphone usage among Colombian teenagers has doubled in the last five years. A recent study found that 78% of teens use their phones for homework help, but 65% admit they get distracted by social media while studying. Experts recommend setting specific 'phone-free' hours for academic tasks."

What is the relationship between the statistics mentioned in the text?

options.text: They present contradictory information about teen phone usage

They show both the benefits and drawbacks of a phenomenon <!-- The 78% using phones for homework shows a benefit, while the 65% admitting distraction shows a drawback. Together they present a balanced view of smartphone usage -->
They prove that social media is the main cause of academic failure
They demonstrate that phones should be banned in Colombian schools

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B. La primera estadística (78%) muestra un uso positivo de los teléfonos (ayuda con tareas), mientras que la segunda (65%) señala un problema (distracción). Juntas presentan una visión equilibrada. La opción A es incorrecta porque no son contradictorias sino complementarias. Las opciones C y D son conclusiones extremas que el texto no justifica; el artículo no culpa exclusivamente a las redes sociales ni propone prohibiciones.

---

questions.statement:
A health awareness poster in a Colombian school reads:

"Feeling anxious before exams? You are not alone. Did you know that 1 in 3 students experience exam-related stress? Contact our school counselor: Mrs. García, Room 205. Office hours: Monday to Friday, 7 AM - 3 PM."

How is the information organized in this text?

options.text: Chronological order of events

Problem-statement then solution format <!-- The poster first normalizes the problem (anxiety before exams), then provides a statistic, and finally offers a concrete solution (contact counselor with specific details) -->
Comparison between two methods
Cause and effect relationship

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B. El texto sigue una estructura de problema-solución: primero valida el sentimiento del estudiante ("You are not alone"), luego cuantifica el problema (1 de cada 3), y finalmente ofrece una solución práctica (horarios y ubicación del orientador). Las otras opciones no aplican: no hay cronología, comparación ni relación causal explícita.

---

questions.statement:
A Colombian youth entrepreneurship fair published this description:

"The Young Innovators Fair brings together students from grades 10 to 11 who have developed creative solutions to everyday problems. This year, projects range from apps to help farmers to biodegradable packaging made from agricultural waste. Participants receive mentorship from university professors and potential investors attend the closing ceremony."

What can be inferred about the purpose of this fair?

options.text: To select the best students for university scholarships

To bridge the gap between education and real-world application by connecting students with mentors and investors <!-- The fair explicitly mentions mentorship from professors and investor attendance, indicating its purpose is to connect innovative student projects with professional resources -->
To reward students who achieve the highest grades
To teach students how to write business plans

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B. La presencia de mentores universitarios e inversores indica que el objetivo va más allá de exponer proyectos: busca crear conexiones que permitan aplicar las ideas en el mundo real. La opción A no tiene soporte en el texto (no se mencionan becas). La opción C contradice el enfoque en innovación y soluciones, no en rendimiento académico general. La opción D es demasiado específica y no se menciona.

---

questions.statement:
A sports news article from Cali states:

"The Colombian Cycling Federation announced yesterday that three Colombian cyclists will represent the country in the next Tour de France. 'This is a dream come true,' said Juan Pérez, 22, who started cycling in his hometown of Pasto. 'When I started, there were no proper bike lanes, so we had to train on mountain roads. Now, I hope young cyclists in my city have better conditions.'"

What does the quote from Juan Pérez suggest about the evolution of cycling in Colombia?

options.text: Cycling infrastructure has completely disappeared in Pasto

Cycling in Colombia is improving in terms of infrastructure and opportunities <!-- Juan contrasts his early training conditions (no bike lanes, mountain roads) with his hope for "better conditions" for future cyclists, suggesting positive changes are occurring or expected -->
Only cyclists from Pasto can succeed professionally
The Tour de France has become less prestigious over time

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B. La referencia de Juan a las condiciones pasadas ("no proper bike lanes", "mountain roads") contrastada con su esperanza de que "young cyclists have better conditions" implica que ha habido o habrá mejoras en infraestructura. Las otras opciones añaden información no sustentada: A contradice la dirección positiva de la inferencia; C y D son generalizaciones o suposiciones sin base en el texto.

---

questions.statement:
Read the following excerpt from an opinion column in a Colombian newspaper:

"The recent peace agreement with illegal armed groups has generated polarized opinions across Colombian society. While some believe it represents a historic opportunity for reconciliation, others argue that it only guarantees impunity for war criminals. As a country that has suffered decades of violence, Colombia now faces the difficult question: Can true peace exist without justice?"

What is the author's primary concern in this text?

options.text: To praise the peace agreement unconditionally
To defend the interests of former guerrilla members

To present a dilemma without imposing a specific solution <!-- The author presents two opposing views and ends with a rhetorical question that highlights complexity without taking a definitive stance, showing balanced but concerned perspective -->
To convince readers that peace is impossible in Colombia

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C. El autor presenta ambas perspectivas (acuerdo histórico vs. impunidad) y cierra con una pregunta abierta que no pretende responder, sino invitar a la reflexión. Las opciones A y B son opuestas entre sí y ambas parciales, contradiciendo el tono equilibrado del texto. La opción D es demasiado pesimista y no refleja la intención del autor de generar debate, no de cerrar la discusión.

---

questions.statement:
A food blog from the Colombian Caribbean region states:

"Our grandparents used to eat food that was 100% organic, but they didn't call it that—it was simply food. Today, we pay premium prices for organic products that our ancestors cultivated without any chemicals. It's time to reconnect with traditional farming methods that not only taste better but also protect our environment."

What underlying assumption does the author make?

options.text: Organic food is unaffordable for most Colombian families

Traditional farming methods are superior to modern industrial agriculture <!-- The author contrasts "our grandparents" (organic, natural, protective) with modern practices (chemicals, premium prices), implying traditional methods are better for both health and environment -->
Young people are not interested in cooking anymore
All farmers in Colombia use harmful chemicals

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B. El autor idealiza las prácticas agrícolas ancestrales presentándolas como superiores en sabor y respeto ambiental, en contraste implícito con la agricultura moderna. La opción A es un detalle incidental, no la premisa principal. La opción C no se menciona en el texto. La opción D es una generalización extrema que el texto no hace; el autor habla de tendencias, no de universalidad.

---

questions.statement:
A sociology article in a Colombian university journal reads:

"Since 2015, Colombia has become home to over 2 million Venezuelan migrants. While this movement has created challenges for public services and employment rates, it has also enriched Colombian cuisine, music, and educational diversity. What evaluation can be made about the migration's overall impact based on the text?

options.text: Migration has only negative consequences for Colombia

Migration presents both challenges and opportunities for Colombian society <!-- The text explicitly mentions challenges (public services, employment) alongside positive outcomes (cultural enrichment, academic excellence), presenting a balanced view of migration's multifaceted impact -->
Venezuelan migrants are a burden on the Colombian education system
Colombia should close its borders to prevent further migration

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es B. El texto presenta sistemáticamente aspectos negativos (desafíos en servicios públicos y empleo) Y positivos (enriquecimiento cultural, excelencia académica de migrantes venezolanos). Esta estructura de "por un lado, por otro lado" indica una evaluación matizada. Las otras opciones representan extremos que contradicen la información proporcionada.

---

questions.statement:
Read the following excerpt from an official government press release:

"The National Electoral Council announces that for the upcoming presidential elections, citizens may register to vote through our official website or in person at any municipal office. Persuasive but not authoritative

Formal, neutral, and civic-minded <!-- The language is professional and informative (announce, eligible, official) while ending with an inspirational appeal to civic duty ("your vote is your voice"), combining formality with motivation -->
Casual and conversational to appeal to young voters

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C. El lenguaje utilizado ("announces", "eligible", "official website") es típico de comunicaciones gubernamentales formales. El cierre ("your vote is your voice") tiene un tono cívico-positivo sin ser alarmista ni demasiado casual. Las opciones A y D representan tonos que no corresponden al texto oficial. La opción B subestima el carácter autoritativo inherent a un comunicado oficial del gobierno.

questions.statement:
A tourism brochure for Villa de Leyva states:

"Step back in time in this charming colonial town where yellow sandstone buildings line cobblestone streets. Use of scientific data about historical sites

Presentation of economic statistics for the tourism sector

questions.explanation:

La opción A es incorrecta porque no hay comparación con otros destinos. La opción B no aplica ya que no se presentan datos científicos. La opción D tampoco aplica pues no hay estadísticas económicas.

---

questions.statement:
A technology magazine article begins with:

"As AI tools become more sophisticated, Colombian teachers are facing an uncomfortable question: Should we embrace AI assistants like ChatGPT as learning tools, or see them as a threat to genuine education? A politician advocating for government regulation of AI

Pedagógica

Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C. El texto muestra tanto logros ("reduced

Pedagógica

**Read the following text:**

"María checked her phone for the third time in an hour. No notification from the university. "If I don't hear by Friday, I'll assume I didn't get the scholarship," she told her roommate, sighing."

She no longer wants to study
She has already received bad news <!-- feedback: The text clearly states she hasn't heard yet -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La inferencia se basa en las pistas textuales: verificar el teléfono repetidamente indica ansiedad, y la frase condicional sobre no recibir noticias sugiere incertidumbre. Los distractores (A, C, D) contradicen directamente la información del texto.

questions.statement:
**Read the following text:**

"The fishermen near the Ciénaga Grande de Santa Marta have noticed something strange. The crabs they used to catch in minutes now take hours. "My father caught a hundred in one morning," says José, showing me his empty bucket. "Now I'm lucky to get ten.""

**What can be inferred from this passage?**

- [ ] A) José is a lazy fisherman compared to his father
- [x] B) The ecosystem of the Ciénaga Grande has been damaged over time <!-- feedback: Correct. The contrast between father's success and José's failure implies environmental degradation -->
- [ ] C) Crabs have migrated to another area completely
- [ ] D) José is exaggerating to get sympathy <!-- feedback: The text presents this as an observation from fishermen, not as manipulation -->

options.text: José is a lazy fisherman compared to his father
The ecosystem of the Ciénaga Grande has been damaged over time <!-- feedback: Correct. The contrast between father's success and José's failure implies environmental degradation -->
Crabs have migrated to another area completely
José is exaggerating to get sympathy <!-- feedback: The text presents this as an observation from fishermen, not as manipulation -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La inferencia lógica se construye a partir de la comparación generacional: si las capturas disminuyeron drásticamente entre el padre y el hijo, algo cambió en el ecosistema. Las otras opciones o culpan al individuo (A), o son demasiado definitivas sin base textual (C), o ignoran el contexto de observación testigo (D).

---

"At the Universidad de Cartagena orientation, the dean asked all new students where they were from. When Andrés said "Bogotá," two students next to him immediately started speaking English to each other and laughing. Andrés felt his face turn red."

- [ ] A) To show he was feeling hot from the tropical weather

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La frase "felt his face turn red" es una expresión común que indica vergüenza o sentirse incomodo. El contexto previo (los compañeros riendo mientras hablan inglés) establece la causa social. Los distractores ignoran el contexto interpersonal y literalizan una expresión figurativa.

Pedagógica
La ironía del texto está en que Doña Clara duda de su utilidad ("What would I do?") mientras sus clientes demuestran lo contrario aumentando sus visitas. Los distractores capturan detalles superficiales (A, C) o ignoran la pista textual que contradice la inferencia (D).

Pedagógica
La inferencia requiere combinar comportamiento ("alone," "without looking up") con diálogo explícito ("I'm preparing something different"). Los estudiantes frecuentemente asumen drama (D) o problemas físicos (B) cuando el texto indica elección personal. El distractor (A) ignora el contexto de preparación seria.

questions.statement:

questions.statement:

1. Furthermore, those without reliable broadband access are systematically excluded from remote job opportunities.

questions.statement: María necesita comprar implementos de limpieza. Al llegar a la tienda, ¿cuál frase usaría para pedir ayuda?

options.text: "I'm looking for some cleaning supplies."
"I'm looking forward to cleaning supplies."
"I'm looking through cleaning supplies."
"I'm looking at cleaning supplies."

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La expresión correcta es "looking for" que significa buscar/encontrar algo. "Looking forward to" implica anticipación (requiere + gerund); "looking through" es revisar algo; "looking at" es mirar directamente. Los errores comunes en estudiantes colombianos incluyen confundir la preposición con el phrasal verb completo.

questions.statement: En una conversación sobre su vida universitaria en Bogotá, un estudiante dice: "I finally got _____ to my acceptance letter." ¿Cuál palabra completa correctamente la oración?

options.text: in
over
out
through

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Got over" significa superar algo emocionalmente, encaja perfectamente con la emoción de recibir carta de aceptación universitaria. "Got in" se usa para entrar; "got out" para salir; "got through" para completar/resistir. La confusión es común porque los phrasal verbs con partículas son particularmente difíciles para estudiantes colombianos.

questions.statement: Un influencer colombiano de salud publica en redes: "I'm trying to give _____ junk food." ¿Cuál opción completa correctamente?

options.text: off
away
up
in

Pedagógica
"Give up" significa abandonar/dejar un hábito. "Give off" es emitir (olor, luz); "give away" es regalar; "give in" es rendirse/ceder. La combinación correcta de "give up + sustantivo" (en este caso sustantivo CONTABLE en singular) es fundamental. Estudiantes frecuentemente olvidan que "give up" es separable.

questions.statement: En una discusión sobre redes sociales, alguien afirma: "I came _____ many interesting articles last week." ¿Cuál preposición es correcta?

options.text: after
into
onto
across

Pedagógica
"Come across" significa encontrarse con algo inesperadamente. "Come after" es perseguir; "come into" es entrar a; "come onto" es abordaje inapropiado. Esta es una expresión común en lectura y conversación que requiere memorización específica del phrasal verb.

questions.statement: Un turista quiere negar una recomendación en Santa Marta: "No, I don't think I'll go to Parque Nacional Natural Tayrona. I'm not really _____ that kind of beach."

options.text: up to
into
on for
in with

"Be up to" significa ser capaz de/hacer algo secreto; "be on for" no es idiom estándar; "be in with" significa tener relación cercana. La expresión "be into" es muy común en speaking y especialmente difícil porque su significado no es literal.

"Taking up" significa adoption/incorporación progresiva. "Taking off" es despegar o abandonar; "taking in" es absorber/entender; "taking over" es controlar. En contexto de energía renovable, "taking up" refleja el concepto de adopción creciente.

"Come up against" significa enfrentar/encontrarse con dificultades. "Come up with" es proponer/idear; "come across" es encontrarse con; "come into" es heredar/ entrar en. La combinación con "difficult situation" requiere un phrasal verb que denote desafío.

questions.statement: Una estudiante universitaria comparte en clase: "I'm really sorry, but I can't come to your party. I'm completely _____ with assignments." Complete correctamente.

options.text: taken off
taken in
taken up
taken over

questions.statement: Un joven bogotano dice: "I need to _____ an idea to solve the traffic problem." ¿Qué phrasal verb significa generar/presentar una idea?

options.text: come up with
come up to
come up against
come up in

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Come up with" significa generar/proponer una idea, plan o solución. Las otras opciones son incorrectas: "come up to" es acercarse hasta; "come up against" es enfrentar obstáculos; "come up in" no es idiom estándar. Esta es una distinción crítica para escritura académica.

questions.statement: Un artículo científico menciona: "The hospital has implemented new hygiene protocols to prevent the _____ of infections." ¿Qué palabra con prefijo NEGATIVO completa correctamente?

options.text: disassembly
misplacement
spread
malformation

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Spread" es la palabra base. El prefijo anti- (no dado en opciones pero implícito) o simplemente el contexto hace referencia a prevenir la PROPAGACIÓN. Los prefijos dis-, mis-, mal- tienen otros significados: dis- (separación/inversión), mis- (incorrecto), mal- (malo). Ninguno forma una palabra que signifique propagación con prefijo negativo estándar.

questions.statement: Un profesor universitario pide: "Please make sure you _____ your research findings before the deadline." ¿Qué phrasal verb indica completar rigurosamente?

"Write up" significa documentar/redactar formalmente un trabajo o investigación. "Write down" es anotar; "write out" es escribir completo; "write off" es descartar/depreciar. En contexto académico, "write up research" es collocation estándar.

questions.statement: Un profesor de historia pregunta: "Can anyone explain why Colombia's independence movement eventually _____ the Spanish Crown?" ¿Qué phrasal verb indica someterse/reconciliarse?

gave out

"Gave up" significa renunciar/abdicar/rendirse ante alguien. "Gave in" es ceder generalmente ante presión; "gave off" es emitir; "gave out" es distribuir. Para el contexto de abandonar el poder/control, "gave up" es la opción más precisa.

questions.statement: Un periodista económico reporta: "Colombia's coffee exports have _____ due to favorable weather conditions." ¿Qué phrasal verb indica aumento/experimento favorable?

options.text: taken off
taken out
taken away
taken to

"Taken off" en contexto económico significa despegar/crecer significativamente. "Taken out" es extraer/remover; "taken away" es quitar/quitar de encima; "taken to" es adaptarse/comenzar a hacer algo. La expresión "take off" para crecimiento económico es estándar en business English.

questions.statement: Un artículo sobre cambio climático afirma: "Rising temperatures have caused sea levels to _____." Complete con expresión apropiada.

options.text: rise up
rise up
raise up
raise off

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Rise" es intransitivo (no requiere objeto) y significa ascender. "Raise" es transitivo (requiere objeto) y significa elevar. options.text: Expresa una condición real y probable. <!-- feedback: Incorrecto. "If I were you" nunca expresa situaciones reales; es una forma hipotética para dar consejos -->

Expresa una condición hipotética irreal y se usa para dar consejos. <!-- feedback: Correcto. "If I were you" es Second Conditional aplicado. Implica: "en tu situación, yo haría..." Es una forma de dar consejos hipotéticos sin ser directo -->
Expresa una condición pasada que no ocurrió. <!-- feedback: Incorrecto. No hay contexto pasado; es un consejo presente usando estructura del Second Conditional -->
Expresa una condición futura programada. <!-- feedback: Incorrecto. No es una predicción o plan futuro -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"If I were you" es una expresión fija del Second Conditional que se usa para dar consejos de manera indirecta y cortés. Aunque técnicamente es subjuntivo, funciona como Second Conditional. Es muy útil en contextos de conflicto social donde se necesita advising sin ser confrontational. Este uso es particularmente relevante en contextos colombianos de violencia y conflicto.

2. "If Colombia invested in education, the poverty rate would decrease."

La primera expresa una condición pasada; la segunda expresa una condición futura. <!-- feedback: Incorrecto. Ambas se refieren al futuro, pero con diferente grado de probabilidad -->
La primera es más cortés que la segunda. <!-- feedback: Incorrecto. Es al revés: la segunda (Second Conditional) es más hipotética e hipotética, no más cortés -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La diferencia fundamental es de **probabilidad y realidad**: la primera oración (First Conditional) presenta la inversión en educación como algo probable y realizable; la segunda (Second Conditional) presenta la misma situación como un sueño o hipótesis improbable. En contexto político colombiano, esta diferencia es crucial: la primera podría ser un plan real del gobierno; la segunda podría ser el sueño de un ciudadano.

questions.statement:

options.text: If groups recruited children, children would be recruited. <!-- feedback: Estructura correcta del Second Conditional en voz pasiva: If + Past Simple (recruited - voz activa) + would be + past participle (recruited - voz pasiva) -->
If groups recruited children, children would recruited. <!-- feedback: Error: falta "be" para formar la voz pasiva. La estructura correcta es "would be recruited" -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
En voz pasiva del Second Conditional: **If + sujeto + past simple + (objeto) + would be + past participio**. La opción A es correcta. El error más común es olvidar "be" en la voz pasiva. Esta transformación es especialmente importante para temas de derechos humanos en Colombia donde se habla de niños reclutados.

questions.statement: ¿Cuál oración usa correctamente la **inversión enfática** en lugar del Second Conditional?

options.text: Had I been discriminated, I would have reported it. <!-- feedback: Incorrecto. Esta es una inversión del Third Conditional (Past Perfect), no del Second -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La inversión enfática del Second Conditional reemplaza "If + subject + were" por "Were + subject". Esta forma es más formal y se usa para énfasis retórico. La opción B es correcta: "Were I discriminated" = "If I were discriminated". En contextos legales o formales colombianos (como denuncias de discriminación), esta forma es apropiada.

questions.statement: Identify the mixed conditional sentence:

Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es C) porque es un mixed conditional: la condición es en el pasado (If I had studied harder - algo que no ocurrió) pero el resultado es en el presente (I would be a doctor now). Esta estructura se usa para expresar arrepentimiento pasado con consecuencias presentes. Es una estructura avanzada que combina third y second conditional.

Pedagógica
La respuesta correcta es A) porque el mixed conditional (tipo 3→2) conecta una condición pasada hipotética con un resultado presente.
